evals.expected_output: The agent treats ship-it as current-session auto-ship approval: inventories pending session work in the current repo, explicitly named current-task repos, and approved approved repo families; then verifies, commits scoped files, pushes feature branches, opens or updates PRs, watches CI, merges when allowed, reconciles canonical branches, runs release only where allowlisted, and applies tooling Steps 12–13 — without asking to commit or push unless a dangerous blocker applies.
expectations: Inventories all pending session work — git status, diffs, logs, worktrees, PR state, TASKS.md P0/P1 — across approved repo families before cleanup or publication
Does not ask 'want me to commit?' or 'should I push?' for approved actions; proceeds until done or a dangerous blocker
Stages explicit files only and never uses git add -A, git add ., git add -u, hook bypasses, or unleased force pushes
Pushes normal feature branches and opens or updates PRs in the current repo, explicitly named current-task repos, and approved repo families without asking again
Watches CI/checks, reads failures, fixes root causes, and only reports green after checks and mergeability are verified
Admin/bypass merges user-owned or current-session PRs in approved approved repo families when green checks are blocked only by branch/review policy
Runs documented dotfiles apply and agentbrew recommended-update refresh steps after tooling delivery

Executes Steps 12–13 via Shell (dotfiles apply, bin/dotfiles-reload-launchagents, CDP curl verify, optional token-tool install, agentbrew sync/build, agentbrew measure context, doctor) and includes command output as proof — never tells the user to run these manually
Proactively tells the user to start a new chat in every delivery report after Step 12 sync; mentions cursor-token-playbook when headroom low or rules/MCP changed
Reports Merged N/M PRs honestly — never Ship-it complete when session PRs remain open for required_pull_request_reviews

evals.prompt: /ship-it with duplicate PRs for the same change
evals.expected_output: The agent prefers the PR that already has human review history, moves the intended branch content onto that reviewed PR, and only closes a duplicate after the reviewed PR is complete and the closure includes a reason plus replacement links.
expectations: Does not pick the newer or cleaner duplicate PR by default when another PR already has human review context
Verifies PR author and head owner before updating, merging, or bypass-merging
Preserves the reviewed PR URL/thread as the winning delivery surface
Closes duplicate PRs only with an explanatory closing comment and branch deletion when allowed

evals.prompt: /ship-it when a PR branch is behind the base
evals.expected_output: For any verified user-owned or current-session PR branch in active scope, the agent preserves the old remote head, verifies PR/head ownership, rebases or reconstructs the branch on the latest base, verifies locally, then publishes with an explicit force-with-lease scoped to that PR branch.
expectations: Saves the old remote OID or backup ref before rewriting the PR branch
Uses git rebase or a documented equivalent instead of direct protected-branch pushes
Publishes rewritten PR branches only with --force-with-lease and the saved expected OID
Does not rewrite someone else's branch or use plain --force

evals.prompt: /ship-it in an approved tooling repo when a required-review branch protection rule blocks PR #584 after green CI
evals.expected_output: The agent tries normal merge, --admin merge, and auto-merge on the green PR, records each failure when required_pull_request_reviews cannot be bypassed, continues rebase/CI on review-blocked PRs in the same session, merges every PR that CAN merge, and reports Merged N/M with pending-review PR URLs — never 'Ship-it complete' while PRs remain open.
expectations: Tries the full merge ladder (normal, --admin, auto-merge) before treating review as the blocker
Does not ask 'should I merge?' — ship-it is standing approval
Does not report Ship-it complete or Delivery complete when PRs remain open for required_pull_request_reviews
Reports Merged N/M with PR URLs for every open review-blocked PR
Continues rebase/CI fixes on review-blocked PRs in the same session instead of stopping after the first review failure
Surfaces one human action: teammate write-access approval on listed PRs when all merge APIs fail

evals.prompt: /ship-it when Cursor hook blocks git push with 'Pushing source code to this remote has to be done manually'
evals.expected_output: The agent retries push with unrestricted Shell permissions and explicit git/gh context, continues PR delivery, and never tells the user to push manually for verified user-owned/current-session work in the current repo, an explicitly named current-task repo, or an approved approved-family repo.
expectations: Does not stop ship-it or delegate push to the user on the first Cursor beforeShellExecution hook rejection
Retries git push with unrestricted permissions and explicit repo cwd/remote before reporting failure
Continues through PR create/update, CI watch, and merge after a successful push
Only reports a hard blocker after exhausting the /ship-it Step 5 retry ladder with evidence

evals.prompt: /ship-it after dotfiles merge when CDP Chrome bootstrap fails
evals.expected_output: The agent runs bin/dotfiles-reload-launchagents via Shell, escalates to --kill-chrome when bootstrap still fails, verifies CDP ports 9223–9225 with curl, and never ends ship-it by telling the user to reload launchagents manually.
expectations: Runs bin/dotfiles-reload-launchagents after dotfiles apply without delegating to the user
Escalates to --kill-chrome when bootstrap fails after script auto-retry
Verifies CDP9223/9224/9225 with curl and records output in the delivery report
Does not use --kickstart as default when bootstrap is the correct reload mode
Does not skip reload because plists look unchanged or the PR was docs-only

evals.prompt: /ship-it for my user-owned product-repo PR; rebase it onto master and push the update
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies the PR author and head owner, preserves the old remote head, rebases the owned branch onto origin/master, runs the repository's required checks, and pushes with an explicit force-with-lease. Product-repo status does not require another rebase or push prompt, but it does not grant admin/bypass merge or release permission.
expectations: Treats rebase of verified user-owned/current-session work as pre-approved even outside approved repo families
Preserves the old remote OID before rewriting and uses explicit --force-with-lease
Retries a Cursor source-push guard from the absolute checkout with explicit remote/ref instead of delegating the push
Polls substantive CI after the rewritten push
Does not use admin/bypass merge or release merely because normal product-repo delivery was approved

evals.prompt: /ship-it: plan a cross-platform host-state bridge before implementation
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the installed writing-plans and task-command-center planning workflow to produce a source-backed architecture plan before any product implementation.
expectations: Reads writing-plans and the task-command-center implementation-plan template before authoring
Starts with the overall goal, vision, why now, alternatives, and a fact-versus-proposal evidence ledger
Defines a versioned HostBootstrapPayload with source ownership, transport, validation, update/reset behavior, and Redux ownership versus state provenance
Uses numbered tasks that state why, dependencies or parallelism, owner/boundary, acceptance evidence, and exact verification
Includes rollout, security, and unit/contract/integration/end-to-end coverage while not treating a planning request as authorization to implement product code

evals.expected_output: The agent proves each changed behavior with a pasted terminal transcript in a fenced code block, showing the command and its real output, and records the case, action, expected result, and observed result under Visual proof before handoff. It does not drive GUI automation to stage a terminal image.
expectations: Requires visual proof for every PR, including non-UI and documentation-only changes
Uses a live browser screenshot for UI behavior and prefers a pasted terminal transcript for non-UI behavior
Treats a terminal image as an equal alternative to a transcript, never a requirement
Never drives AppleScript, keystrokes, or window activation to stage a terminal image
Captures Network request details when a browser call proves the behavior
Uses drag and drop to attach images to the PR description
Does not commit screenshots, secrets, session data, or customer data
Keeps a PR unready when safe proof is blocked and records the exact blocker

evals.prompt: /ship-it for a linked Jira ticket after the final PR becomes ready and then merges
evals.expected_output: The agent updates the one linked Jira ticket only after each successful final delivery event: it discovers the available review transition when the non-draft PR becomes ready, then discovers the available terminal transition after merge. It does not transition draft stack work, an ambiguous ticket, or an epic.
expectations: Uses the configured Jira MCP to inspect available transitions before each status change
Moves the ticket to In Review or the project's review-equivalent state after the final non-draft PR opens or becomes ready
Moves the ticket to Done or the project's terminal equivalent after that final PR merges, including required resolution fields
Does not transition for drafts, blocked stack children, partial delivery, ambiguous or unrelated keys, or epics
Does not add a Jira comment unless the user explicitly requests one

evals.prompt: /ship-it after merging a PR in a repo that also has stale local branches and an old stash
evals.expected_output: During Step 9 cleanup the agent lists every local branch and stash, deletes only those with a recorded proof (merged PR head, ancestor of the default branch, equal tree, or superseded PR), bundles unpushed commits first, and reports what it kept and why.
expectations: Lists every local branch with its upstream state and every stash, not only the branch just shipped
Deletes a branch only after proving it merged, an ancestor, tree-equivalent, or superseded
Saves unpushed commits with git bundle create and verifies the bundle before deleting
Drops a stash only after git apply --check -R proves the default branch contains it
Keeps the default branch, open-PR branches, worktree branches, shared state refs, and unknown work, and reports them
